Insignificant · battle timeline replayer

The whole roster, replayed from the core's own timeline

One full-roster battle per era, replayed. Every hit, miss, dodge, interception, disable, repair and shoot-down below was resolved by core/battle.gd in a headless run, exported to a tick-stamped timeline by tools/export_timeline.gd, and embedded in this file. There is no combat code on this page. It stages the 掩護鏈 of ADR-0008 — 近戰列 → 工事線 → 遠程列 → 空域, each layer screening the one behind it — under the top-down camera of ADR-0009, and it plays back what the engine did. Each fighter is one static sprite; all the motion is cheap transforms.

A replayer, not a simulator

The page holds no rule. It reads a tick-stamped event list — take_station, hit, miss, dodge, death, intercept, disable, shootdown, repair, medal — and animates each entry at the tick it carries. It cannot drift from the rules, because it has nothing to drift with.

source: docs/fixtures/battle_timeline.json

掩護鏈: front to back

自動佈陣 places four layers, front (midline) to back: 近戰列 → 工事線 → 遠程列 → 空域, and each screens the one behind it. Units walk to their station and hold it — nobody chases anything here, because the standing arrangement is the cover.

ADR-0008

盾陣 screens the 遠程列

One card is one wall segment spanning the ranged row's frontage, which is why it draws as a run of wall rather than a single block. It intercepts one 近戰 attack aimed at that row and nothing else: an attack on the 近戰列 lands in front of it, and a shot at 空域 bypasses the 工事線 entirely.

攔截 · 失效 · 修復

工兵團 stands behind the wall

The engineer stations in the 遠程列 and works at the 工事線: the wall it repairs is the wall covering it. One repair per round, taking turns over the line, and it never attacks.

ADR-0007 + ADR-0008

正規軍 field screens too

A 正規軍 wave that brings a 遠程列 unit brings the 盾陣 that covers it, so 火砲's 「可癱瘓敵方工事」 finally has something to bust. They field no 防空飛彈 and have no 工兵團 — strip an enemy screen and it stays down. That asymmetry is the engineer line's whole value.

敵方的工事永不修復

Cover reads by position alone

No cover indicator, no label, no highlight. The top-down camera exists so that 「this wall stands in front of those archers」 is something you simply see. If the arrangement does not read, that is a finding, not a missing overlay.

ADR-0009

Real numbers, real rolls

攻 and 血 are the catalog's values × that era's coefficient (1/2/3/5/8/12). The quality three are a real acquisition roll on the cards track; the enemy carries the engine defaults (命中 100%, 閃避 0%, 攻速 1.0) exactly as 戰鬥.md says every opponent does.

seeded, reproducible

Static sprite, cheap motion

Each unit is a single PNG. Facing is an X flip, walking to station is a position tween, and liveliness is a sine bob. No walk-cycle frames exist, which is the point.

0 animation frames

What this is. The prototype of the battle scene W15 builds in-engine. Its top-down camera is the game's battle camera (docs/adr/0009-the-battle-scene-is-top-down.md), and watching the roster resolve on an earlier build of this page is what surfaced the cover defect that became the ordered cover chain (docs/adr/0008). The Godot battle scene will replay the same event contract from the same core, so anything that reads badly here reads badly there.

How the fixture is made. tools/export_timeline.gd runs one 世界大戰-typed battle per era — the uncapped type, so it settles the moment the field can no longer change — with the player fielding one card per era-legal unit class plus its whole 工事線, and the enemy fielding one 正規軍 per era-legal roster type plus the 盾陣 its wave brings. Skill cards are left out: they have no station in the chain and nothing to render. Re-running the exporter and diffing is part of Part A, so a rule change that moves the timeline cannot leave this page stale.

One unit per class per side is load-bearing. Timeline labels are card ids, so two 步兵團 on one side would share one label — architecture.md is explicit that labels are not identities. The fixtures give every unit a unique label per side, which is what lets this page key its handles off (side, label) at all.

Deliberate presentation choices (the events are the game's, the staging is this page's):

  • Positions are invented here. core/battle.gd has no coordinates: a unit's only spatial attribute is its categorical row, plus — for the 遠程列 — the card id of the wall screening it, which arrives as take_station. The columns, the lanes, the walk-in and the wall's tiled frontage are all this page's staging of that.
  • A round is stretched to 4.5 s. 攻 and 血 both scale by the era coefficient, so a strike is worth one or two units' whole HP at every era. Ticks map linearly onto those 4.5 s, so an event at tick 74 lands three quarters of the way through the window.
  • Flight time is cosmetic. Core resolves a strike atomically at its tick. Here a thrown weapon gets travel time and its damage number lands on impact; a death waits for the projectile that killed it so an aircraft is not gone before the missile arrives.
  • No 軍費 decisions, no waves, no growth loop. The whole roster is committed at the opening boundary and the battle runs to its end. What the fixture does record — 本場已燒軍費 and 戰功 — is shown on the closing card.
  • The enemy's era forms are drawn with the same sprites as ours, mirrored. A per-side art split is a W14.8 question, not a rule.

Unit assets used on this page

Every sprite here is an exploratory raw from assets/exploration/topdown-demo/, never a pipeline asset: none of them are in assets/approved/, and neither inventory.md nor the style bible knows about them. Rendered with the locked recipe (Krea-2-Turbo + Moebius LoRA @1.0, euler/simple, 8 steps, cfg 1.0) at seed 501, plus five review re-rolls at seed 403; prompt and seed for all 60 are recorded in docs/tools/topdown_demo_sprites.json. Embedded here at 256px and 128 colours with the grey render background keyed out. Columns are the per-class era forms the fixtures actually put on the field (so this table, like the field, holds no catalog transcription of its own); a dash means that class has no form in that era, so no sprite was rendered. The three exceptions are 防空飛彈 era 1–3 (擋箭棚／箭樓／城防塔): those renders exist and are still embedded in this file, but the forms themselves were retired by ADR-0006 (有空軍才有防空), so the table shows a dash and no fixture ever places them.

Flying weapons

Projectile art has no era of its own: one sprite per ammunition type, mapped onto classes and eras by this page's AMMO table. All authored pointing right, except the bomb, authored nose-down for its vertical fall.
